answer: A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases hence has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Because the vault collateral is checked against the orchard claim at intake, the copper audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 2 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 18 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
